question: Should memory-wiki vault isolation be solved through generic agent-scoped plugin config, a memory-wiki-specific per-agent vault map, context-aware vault path templates, or a different maintained vault-selection contract?
rationale: The current gap is real, but the implementation choice sets security-sensitive plugin config/API and durable memory isolation behavior that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Design generic agent-scoped plugin config
options.body: Add a reusable agents.list/defaults plugin-config override contract and make memory-wiki consume it for vault routing while preserving one global default path for upgrades.

options.title: Add memory-wiki-specific vault routing
options.body: Keep the generic plugin config surface unchanged and add a narrow memory-wiki map/template mechanism for per-agent vault selection.

options.title: Defer to broader config tracker
options.body: Keep this issue linked to the generic per-agent plugin config tracker and close or pause memory-wiki-specific work until that contract is chosen.

recommendation.title: Design generic agent-scoped plugin config
recommendation.body: Add a reusable agents.list/defaults plugin-config override contract and make memory-wiki consume it for vault routing while preserving one global default path for upgrades.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking choice is primarily a plugin/config contract and agent schema decision rather than only a memory-wiki implementation detail.
